reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the pair, returned to the formal regulations on core requirements, concentration and Capstone, the named UCV module list and current catalogue descriptions. Reconstructed the eight credit groups from their controlling provisions. Rechecked the 2.5 EC Portfolio against the summary and the research progression against course prerequisites. Rechecked workbook evidence and semester eligibility for the affected UCR placements and the closest comparison. Compared the results against the exact frozen pair in a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The single-concentration illustration totals 180 EC. It includes 20 core-course EC, 20 introductory core skills/project EC, 2.5 final-year Portfolio EC, 15 general education EC, 75 concentration-course EC, 12.5 concentration skills EC, 15 concentration project EC and 20 Capstone EC. Article 3.8 gives 20 EC for the combined core skills and projects, while the itemised Appendix and catalogue agree on the 2.5 EC advanced core Portfolio in addition to the 20 EC introductory set. The illustration follows the named entries, explicitly retaining that reporting discrepancy. It does not assert that the three thematic pillars are separate regulatory concentrations. Article 3.8 gives 10–20 EC general education for a single concentration, with at least one humanities and one alternate-domain course, or 10 EC of humanities for interdisciplinary study. Article 3.9 gives 70–80 EC concentration courses, at least 20 advanced across at least three courses and at most 20 introductory. One of three concentration projects must be advanced.

The introductory Applied Researcher I–III sequence develops a proposal, collects data, then analyses results in R and communicates findings in a group article and a poster. Applied Researcher II requires I, and III requires I and II. The advanced Portfolio is pass/fail and is listed from semester 5, with reflections drawn from the three years. The Capstone is a final scholarly project with entry after 140 EC. The separate Food in Transition project applies systems thinking to an interdisciplinary food challenge.

Both the external credit illustration and each UCR plan total 180 EC. The scheduled qualitative research course includes a team inquiry and reporting after foundational methods. The biology and behaviour directions are distinct applications of the verified themes. The research sequence and specialist food courses clarify the limits of the comparison. The required Capstone and UCR optional research remain separate.
